tools.name: Apple Notes
tools.description: Read and write notes in Apple Notes. List, search, create, update, append and delete notes and folders.

tools.name: Apple Reminders
tools.description: Manage Apple Reminders — list, create, complete, delete and search reminders across all lists.

tools.name: Audio
tools.description: Exposes macOS audio as live MCP resources that push on change: output volume/mute (resource://audio/output), input (mic) volume/mute (resource://audio/input), and the device inventory with each device's live volume/mute + current defaults (resource://audio/devices). Tools: get/set output & input volume + mute (targeting the default device or any specific device by UID), and list / switch the default output & input device.

tools.name: Bash / Shell
tools.description: Run shell commands and scripts on macOS. Capture stdout/stderr, open interactive Terminal windows, and automate system tasks. Also starts long-running processes by handle and exposes each one's live status as a subscribable resource (resource://bash/process/{id}), so a button face can reflect whether a process is running.

tools.name: Google Chrome
tools.description: Control Chrome tabs and windows via JXA. Optionally enable CDP (--remote-debugging-port=9222) for JS execution, page source, and screenshots.

tools.name: Clipboard
tools.description: Read, write, transform, and manage the macOS system clipboard. Supports plain text, HTML, RTF, file paths, and clipboard history.

tools.name: Filesystem
tools.description: Read, write, edit, move and search files and directories on disk. Wraps the official @modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem — every operation is confined to the folders you allow, and paths outside them are refused. Set the allowed roots in this pack's config before use.

tools.name: Launcher
tools.description: Open apps, folders, URLs and reveal files in Finder using the macOS open command.

tools.name: Memory
tools.description: A persistent key-value store for buttons — the one thing a face cannot do for itself. A face runs on an opaque origin with no localStorage and no indexedDB, and its local view state dies when the idle window is dismissed, so without a server a button cannot remember anything between presses. Get/set/delete any JSON value, plus increment_value and toggle_value for the two cases buttons actually need (a press counter, a latching toggle). The whole store is also a live resource (resource://memory/store), so a face can bind it and repaint when a value changes.

tools.name: Obsidian
tools.description: Read and write notes in your Obsidian vault. Search by content, create and update notes, manage folders, and navigate your vault structure.

tools.name: OpenAI
tools.description: Structured LLM calls, image analysis (GPT-4o vision), image generation and editing (GPT Image — written to disk and returned as a path, never as inline base64), and Whisper audio transcription. All tools share a single API key.

tools.name: Photoshop
tools.description: Drive Adobe Photoshop by script — 100 tools covering documents, layers (create/order/transform/properties/masks), selections, text, filters, colour adjustments, layer styles, history, actions, data sets, image stacks, export/place, and the generative-AI family (fill, remove, expand, upscale, sky replacement, generate image). Includes 16 multi-step recipe tools that run a whole workflow (remove background, enhance portrait, frequency separation, batch watermark, CSV to cards…) inside one suspended history state, so a single Undo reverts the lot. Works by running ExtendScript inside Photoshop over AppleScript's `do javascript`, with no plugin to install. Also exposes the active document's live state as a subscribable resource (resource://photoshop/document) plus key, dial and popup surfaces.

tools.name: PowerPoint
tools.description: Drive the open Microsoft PowerPoint presentation via AppleScript — read the live selection, restyle selected shapes and text, add text boxes and shapes, create/delete/duplicate/reorder slides, navigate the editor, and run the slide show as a presenter remote (start/exit, next/previous, jump to slide, elapsed time). Also exposes the open presentation and the live selection as subscribable resources (resource://powerpoint/presentation, resource://powerpoint/selection) plus key, dial and popup surfaces.

tools.name: QuickTime Player
tools.description: Control QuickTime Player via AppleScript. Record audio (microphone → M4A) and screen (full screen → MOV), open media files, and list open documents. On first use macOS will ask permission to control QuickTime — click Allow once.

tools.name: Safari
tools.description: Control Safari tabs and windows via AppleScript. Includes JS execution, page source and text via 'Allow JavaScript from Apple Events' (no extension or debug port needed).

tools.name: Screenshot
tools.description: Capture the screen, frontmost window, a clicked window, or an interactive drag-selected region as a PNG image. Saves to a path (creating folders as needed) or returns base64. Also records the screen to video.

tools.name: VS Code
tools.description: Control VS Code windows — toggle sidebar/terminal/panels, run commands, create terminals, open folders. Requires the 'nicollasr.vscode-streamdeck' extension installed in VS Code.

tools.name: Web
tools.description: Search the web and read pages. search_web and search_news query the Brave Search API (needs a free API key); fetch_url retrieves any http(s) page and returns it as readable text, and needs no key at all. fetch_url is also how a face reaches an HTTP API it cannot call itself — a face runs on an opaque origin, so its own fetch is blocked by CORS for most hosts, while a pack request carries no Origin.

tools.name: Window Management
tools.description: Move, resize and snap windows across screens; open, close and place windows across displays and spaces. The tools ACT; the observable state is subscribable resources — the app list, the open windows, the displays, the Mission Control spaces and the frontmost app, each with a schema a face can bind to. Windows are addressed by stable handles (get_windows and new_window return one per window) rather than by a z-order index that shifts as windows are focused. Multi-monitor aware: a new window lands on the display the pointer is on rather than wherever the app cascaded it, and any window can be pulled to the display in front of you. Also ships an app-switcher across three Stream Deck surfaces — a key (press cycles apps), a dial (rotate to preview, press to switch), and a popup grid — as live MCP App UI resources with in-component handlers.

tools.name: Xcode
tools.description: Drive the running Xcode session via AppleScript — build, run, test, clean and stop the active scheme, read structured build errors/warnings/test failures, switch schemes, inspect projects/targets/build settings, open files and jump to a line. Also exposes the active workspace's live build state as a subscribable resource (resource://xcode/build) plus key, dial and popup surfaces.
